rappel_detail.anchor: slings and rap rings on a tree
rappel_detail.station: The marked south-facing gully (the southern chimney) south of the summit, reached by traversing back past the false summits; the anchor is a tree rigged with slings and rings at its top.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 3, single rope, down the drippy, dank chimney.

rappel_detail.anchor: slings and rings on a tree or chockstone
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 3, single rope, to the foot of the chimney.

rappel_detail.anchor: slings at the head of the snow finger
rappel_detail.station: The foot of the chimney, above the snow finger.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 3 of 3, down the steep, narrow snow finger below the chimney, back to the basin.
hazards: Seasonal snow: early in the year this is steep snow; later it may be loose rock and scree. Carry extra webbing and rap rings, since the slings are replaced only by passing parties.

set.rappels: 3 rappels from the slung tree in the marked gully south of the summit (the second gully heading east past the false summits): two in the chimney, one down the snow finger, then scree back to Thumbtack Rock
set.rappel_count_note: The standard summer descent: two single-rope rappels down the marked southern chimney, then a third down the snow finger below it. Anchors are slings and rings on trees and chockstones; carry spare webbing.
